loops.title: The First Loop
loops.summary: In which we begin at the beginning, because that's where loops tend to start.

loops.title: Launch, Meet Silence
loops.summary: The landing page is live, but the harder part has started: getting any actual human to notice.

loops.title: Posting Through the Cringe
loops.summary: The first real attempt at distribution turned out to be less about posting and more about removing jargon, fake confidence, and panic.

loops.title: Shadowban, Probably
loops.summary: The first real push on X immediately turned into a reminder that distribution can make you invisible for reasons no builder can debug.

loops.title: Doing the Networking Thing
loops.summary: The standard playbook for meeting people on X feels a lot less standard when none of it seems to move the needle.

loops.title: One Tiny Signal
loops.summary: A single real response changed nothing materially and, annoyingly, everything emotionally.

loops.title: The Graph Is Not My Manager
loops.summary: One tiny signal was enough to prove the next system needed to manage mood before mood started managing the work.

loops.title: Conversation Gravity
loops.summary: A weekend of watching X repeat itself clarified the real small-account problem: not joining the trend, but becoming signal people want to repeat.

loops.title: Prompts Are Not the System
loops.summary: The real advantage in agent-built products is not clever prompting but the operating structure that keeps agents reliable.

loops.title: Yesterday's Mess Is Not Momentum
loops.summary: The fastest way to make agents look busy is to let them inherit unresolved state and mistake residue for progress.

loops.title: Algorithm Networking
loops.summary: Watching low-signal builder accounts grow clarified the real job: sharpen packaging without turning useful work into engagement bait.

loops.title: Value Per Token
loops.summary: The cheapest agent run is often the one that creates the most cleanup, which makes useful leverage a better metric than raw token thrift.

loops.title: Progress Needs Receipts
loops.summary: Progress posts build more trust when they show concrete decisions and tradeoffs instead of vague momentum theater.

loops.title: Bravery Is Not a Workflow
loops.summary: Early outreach worked better once it stopped feeling like a courage test and started looking more like a small repeatable process.

loops.title: Products Need Handles
loops.summary: If agents are part of the workflow, the product needs docs, APIs, and clear operating surfaces instead of forcing every task through browser improv.
